sentences.text: on 12 August, 2024
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C. V. Bhaskar Reddy

Writ Petition No.13740 of 2015
Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioner, seeking the following relief:
"...to issue a Writ or order direction more particularly on in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of respondents in not paying the compensation of Rs.10,08,919/- for the purpose of acquiring the petitioners property to an extent of 40.06 situated at Plot No.19 in Sy.No.94 & 95 house bearing No.18-1-554/B/7 at Kandikal gate, Uppuguda, Hyderabad and contrary to the provision of GHMC Act and the principles of natural justice and consequentially direct the respondent No.4 to release the award amount Rs.10,08,919/- in favour of petitioner and pass..."

2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.

The case of the petitioner is that he is the absolute owner and possessor of land to an extent of 333 sq.yards in Plot No.19 in Sy.No.s.94 and 95, situated at Kandikal Gate, Uppuguda, Hyderabad having purchased the said land under a registered sale deed vide document dated 21.02.1985.

It is the further case of the petitioner that the said land was acquired by the respondents for the purpose of widening the road from Durdana Hotel to Chandrayan Gutta Police Station via Keshavagiri junction by issuing draft notification, Notification No.Hyd/141, dated 23.08.2013.

Thereafter, draft declaration was issued on 13.11.2013 vide declaration No.Hyd/181 and an Award was also passed vide proceedings No.A/623/2013, dated 13.12.2013 for the value of Rs.4,96,282/-.
4.

It is further case of the petitioner that subsequently the respondents have issued Form No.9 Notice under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (1 of 1894), dated 23.01.2014 awarding an amount of Rs.12,70,679.89 for the acquired property and after deducting income tax at the rate of 20.6% from the awarded compensation granted net amount of Rs.10,08,919/-.
5.

The grievance of the petitioner is that he made a representation to respondent No.4 on 10.04.2015 stating that the awarded compensation was not released in his favour till date and requested him to initiate appropriate steps for payment of the said compensation amount.
However, respondent No.4 did not act upon the said representation; the present writ petition is filed.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contended that the land of the petitioner was acquired vide notification dated 28.08.2013 for the purpose of widening of road.

Learned counsel further contended that even after concluding the award proceedings on 23.01.2014, no Sadath Ali Baig S/O Late Late Ma. Khader ... vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85352483/
1 compensation amount has been paid to the petitioner.

sentences.text: 6. This writ petition is pending on the file of this Court from the year 2015.
Till date, no counter-affidavit has been filed by the respondents.

7. In view of the said submissions, the respondents are directed to forthwith release the compensation amount payable to the petitioner in pursuance of the award proceedings No.A/623/2013, dated 13.12.2013 and also the Notice of award dated 23.01.2014, within a period of three (03) months from today.

Since it is the case of the petitioner that his livelihood has been affected by forcible acquisition of his land, deduction of income tax amount and not releasing the compensation amount, this Court is of the view that the ends of justice would be met if the writ petition is allowed with costs of Rs.1,00,000/-, payable by the respondents besides depositing the amount as per the award proceedings.
8. With the above observations/directions, this Writ Petition is allowed.

As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
